subject: mathematics
question_text: Let a = i + j + k and b = 2i + 3j + k. Find the vector component of b perpendicular to a, and the component of b on a.

mark_split.label: Find the component of b on a
Find the vector component along a
Subtract to get the perpendicular part

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), chapter 7 PRODUCT OF VECTORS, Short Answer question 35(ii), book p.74. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. READING OF THE STEM: the question asks two different things about the same pair, and they use the two different forms of the projection. 'The component of b on a' is the SCALAR (a·b)/|a| = 6/√3 = 2√3 ≈ 3.464; 'the vector component of b perpendicular to a' is the VECTOR b − ((a·b)/|a|²)a. Part (i) of the same book question asked for the projection vector and is authored separately as ts_ipe_m1a_pv_projection_vector_ijk_2i3jk, so this card recomputes the along-a part rather than pointing at the other card, and states in words which form is which. Computed twice. Symbolically: a·b = 6, |a|² = 3, along-a part = 2(i + j + k), perpendicular part = b − 2(i + j + k) = (2−2)i + (3−2)j + (1−2)k = j − k. By direct check: (j − k)·(i + j + k) = 0 + 1 − 1 = 0, so the perpendicular part really is perpendicular; and 2(i + j + k) + (j − k) = 2i + 3j + k = b, so the two parts reassemble b. The scalar 2√3 also equals |2i + 2j + 2k| = √12 = 2√3, as it must. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1+1+1 split rewards the four separate acts: the two ingredients, the scalar component, the vector along a, and the subtraction. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B runs Q11 to Q18 at 4 marks each, answer any 6 of 8, under the 2026-27 pattern; Product of Vectors carries a Section B slot on the paper and also appears in Section C. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would split b into a part along a and a part perpendicular to a — name each move in order.

steps.label: Find a·b and |a|
steps.margin_note: First mark. Both answers come from the same two numbers, so compute them once. Note both |a| and |a|² — the scalar form uses |a| and the vector form uses |a|².
steps.memory_tip: One dot product and one length serve both answers.
lines: a = i + j + k,  b = 2i + 3j + k

accept: a dot b is six and mod a is root three
the dot product is six and the squared length is three
compute both ingredients before splitting b
a dot b six, mod a root three, mod a square three
find the dot product and the length of a first

steps.why: Both the scalar component and the vector component are built from the same dot product; only the denominator changes. Computing them once makes the difference between the two forms visible.
common_mistakes: Recording only |a| and then needing |a|² later without noticing.

steps.label: Component of b on a
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The COMPONENT of b on a is a number, not a vector: it is the length of b's shadow on a. Its formula divides by |a|, one power only.
steps.memory_tip: Component means a NUMBER: divide by |a|, one power only.
lines: The component of b on a is a number:
it is the length of the shadow of b

recall.must_convey: That the component of b on a is the scalar (a·b)/|a| = 6/√3 = 2√3.
accept: the component on a is a dot b divided by mod a
six over root three is two root three
this one is a number not a vector
component ante number, six by root three, two root three
rationalise six over root three to get two root three

steps.why: Dividing by |a| once turns a into a unit vector, and a dot product with a unit vector is exactly the length of the shadow. A second division would shrink it wrongly.
common_mistakes: Dividing by |a|² and getting 2, which is the scale factor, not the component.
Giving a vector when a number was asked for.

steps.label: Vector component along a
steps.margin_note: Third mark. This is the VECTOR form, so it divides by |a|² and keeps a. It is needed only as a stepping stone to the perpendicular part.
steps.memory_tip: Vector form divides by |a|² and keeps a; scalar form divides by |a| and drops a.
lines: The vector component of b along a

recall.must_convey: That the vector component of b along a is (6/3)a = 2i + 2j + 2k.
accept: the vector along a is six over three times a
two i plus two j plus two k
this form divides by mod a squared and keeps the vector a
vector form lo mod a square tho divide chesi a ni unchali
the part of b lying along a is twice a
heard_as: two i two j two k

steps.why: Any vector splits into exactly one piece along a given direction and one piece at right angles to it. This is the first piece, and the second is whatever is left when it is taken away.
common_mistakes: Reusing 2√3 here, which is the scalar and not the vector.
Multiplying by b instead of a.

steps.label: Subtract for the perpendicular part
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Subtract the along-a part from b itself. The check costs one line and catches any slip: the result must dot to zero with a.
steps.memory_tip: Perpendicular part = b minus the part along a.

recall.must_convey: That b minus the along-a part gives j − k, whose dot product with a is zero, and that the two answers are j − k and 2√3.
accept: subtract two i two j two k from b to get j minus k
the perpendicular component is j minus k
check it by dotting with a and getting zero
b nunchi along part teesesthe j minus k vasthundi
the two answers are j minus k and two root three

steps.why: b is the sum of its along-a part and its perpendicular part, so removing one leaves the other. The dot product with a is zero, which is what proves the leftover really is perpendicular.
common_mistakes: Subtracting b from the along-a part, which reverses every sign.
Reporting only one of the two things the question asks for.
